title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER
candidates.premise: The highway through the Orrin Cut is the only way out of a flooding river region, and for six weeks drivers have reported walls of cold air that are not there; four road workers have been hurt by something nobody can see. Surveyor Ilse Brandvold finds that the cut slices through Sheaf, a country that lives in one thin plane, whose streets are halved every time a truck crosses. Sheaf's civic speaker, Vesh, perceives people only as sudden blades, and the governor wants nine thousand evacuation vehicles through in twelve days. Illuminara can hold a lane open, but she cannot perceive a plane she has no sense for.

candidates.title: THE PARLIAMENT OF THE TIDAL FLAT
candidates.premise: On the salt flats of Merrin Sound lives the Reeve, a layered colony of worm, alga and silt that has deliberated for two centuries on whether the shore may be walled; it votes by tide, and each year it quietly shifts its channels so that every wall silts up. The fishing town of Dunmere, eight thousand people, needs a sea wall before the autumn surge in twenty-four days, and the harbour board has ordered the flat dredged. Clam-warden Hollis Frayne can read the Reeve's channel patterns better than anyone alive; Illuminara can hold back water for a night, not a season.

candidates.title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT
candidates.premise: On the island of Skerrow a surge is forecast in nine days, and the old ferry is condemned; three hundred and ten islanders will need a vessel that can cross open water and also beach on a shingle bank. The island's two boatyards, the Oyelaran yard, which builds deep keels for rough sea, and the Fenn yard, which builds flat hulls for shallow landings, have not shared a slip in thirty years. Each master says the other's design would sink the boat. Illuminara can hold a hull steady while it is joined, but she cannot design what two stubborn masters will not draw together.

candidates.title: THE ROPE BETWEEN TWO PHILOSOPHIES
candidates.premise: On the north ridge of Kestrel Fang a storm pins two parties at nearly seven thousand metres: six clients under guide Torvald Brekke, who relies on fixed ropes, and four climbers under Zuri Okonjo-Pell, who refuses any rope she has not placed herself. A client is hanging in a crevasse and a descent line of eleven hundred metres is needed in fourteen hours. Illuminara can shield one ledge from the wind for a limited time, but she cannot carry ten people down a mountain.

candidates.title: THE CIRCLE THAT LENT ON NOTHING BUT FACES
candidates.premise: In Larkspur Quarter six hundred night-market traders borrow their stock money from rotating savings circles that run on a handful of tally-cords and the memory of Mama Nneka Orsolo, who has kept them for forty years. After a rumour that she lost a pot to a cousin, three circles call in their pots on the same day, and the quarter's working money will vanish in four market days. The city offers formal loans at a rate no stall can bear. Illuminara can sit all night with the cords, but she cannot make people trust a memory.

candidates.title: THE KEEPER OF THE GALACTIC NOON
candidates.premise: Every ship in the Orrery Reach, forty thousand worlds, sets its clock by the Noon, a time signal derived from one pulsar by a single observatory on the dwarf world Teth. Its keeper, Ketil Amadi-Ross, seventy-eight, has refused for decades to let the Navigators' Guild take over the computation; now the pulsar has begun to glitch, ship clocks are drifting apart, and in fourteen days the Meridian Throat, a junction crowded by thousands of ships, will have vessels disagreeing about the hour by up to a minute. Illuminara can hold a lane open for a short time, but she cannot hold a galaxy's clock.

candidates.title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
candidates.premise: A cruiser of the Marin Concord has blockaded the harbour of Calder, sixty thousand people, until the harbourmaster hands over a refugee ship. At the table the harbourmaster's refusal is flat. His delegation's nineteen-year-old interpreter, Bram Ivarsson, has been ordered to render it as we are considering it, to buy a night. The Concord's captain, Anselm Vey, has announced that a maybe will be taken as a yes and a no will be taken as the end of talks. Illuminara has no standing at the table and cannot speak for either side.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD THE FIRE WAS COMING FOR
candidates.premise: On Cinder Ridge seventy-one-year-old Mireille Dusk has refused every evacuation order for her four hundred trees, each planted by her late husband on a child's birthday. A fire front is thirty hours away and forty homes lie behind her ridge. The brigade chief, Bastien Olsen, wants her down by dark. Illuminara can hold a firebreak for a few hours, not thirty, and she cannot make a woman leave what she loves.

candidates.title: THE JUROR WHO WOULD NOT SIGN
candidates.premise: In the hill court of Sennet twelve neighbours must be unanimous to convict, and eleven say that farmer Kaspar Welle diverted a stream during the drought. The twelfth, retired teacher Edda Moravec, will not sign and will not say why. The sentence under the court's old rule is exile from the valley, and his dairy would fail within a season; the drought water hearing is tomorrow. Illuminara has been invited to sit as an observer, not a juror, and has no authority in the room.

candidates.title: THE SENTENCE SHE FINISHED FOR THE CHILD
candidates.premise: A storm will break over the lower district of Brindle in five hours, and nine-year-old Odette Marchetti insists the school culvert will flood. Illuminara, who understands quickly and has a habit of finishing people's sentences, tells the engineers what the child means, and she is wrong. The crew sandbags the wrong channel. By the time she notices, there are ninety minutes left, and she has to stop guessing and let a child finish.

selection.title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
selection.reason: The best closing contrast is a room in which a single word can start a bombardment and the youngest person has the decisive choice. Bram is not merely a conduit: he must refuse an order to falsify Quillan's answer while preserving a path Captain Vey can honestly report. Illuminara has no standing and succeeds only by listening, clarifying what each party can genuinely offer and helping Bram design read-back and alternatives without speaking for him. Exact language, medical access, inspection and a dawn meeting turn empathy into verifiable procedure, while refugees, harbour residents, the captain and the interpreter all retain real vetoes and consequences.
selection.risk: The ending will feel facile if an interpreter simply appends three concessions and a blockading captain accepts them because they sound reasonable. The author should establish who authorises each offer, let Bram request and receive explicit delegation, use read-back on both sides, and give Vey a coherent security belief and a concrete command constraint. The neutral inspection must protect refugee identity and consent rather than make vulnerable people bargaining material. A bounded first medical landing or inspection should prove that the corridor works before the blockade moves. Keep the possibility of refusal live, explain why the stand-off distance changes immediate fire risk, and let Bram's dismissal and the unresolved blockade remain real rather than rewarding honesty with instant peace.

rounds.summary: The best closing contrast is a room in which a single word can start a bombardment and the youngest person has the decisive choice. Bram is not merely a conduit: he must refuse an order to falsify Quillan's answer while preserving a path Captain Vey can honestly report. Illuminara has no standing and succeeds only by listening, clarifying what each party can genuinely offer and helping Bram design read-back and alternatives without speaking for him. Exact language, medical access, inspection and a dawn meeting turn empathy into verifiable procedure, while refugees, harbour residents, the captain and the interpreter all retain real vetoes and consequences.

AUTHOR_DRAFT of S3 from selected candidate C07, written against the biggest risk named in B01. Delegation is explicit: Bram asks Quillan to say each offer aloud and reads each back, and Quillan agrees only to what he names. Vey has a concrete command constraint (fire unless he holds a verifiable answer to the weapons-and-one-man claim), so the doors answer his real rule rather than sounding reasonable. The neutral inspector reports in signed writing and a Concord observer stays on the quay. Refugees keep agency: Illuminara carries only what Sefa authorises after a hand vote; no names leave the ship; the rifles claim is true and is declared by Sefa first. A bounded first step (the medical landing at nine) precedes the stand-off to six kilometres. Remaining costs: Bram is dismissed from the delegation, Quillan resents the inspection, one voter on the ship stays angry, the blockade remains at distance. Outcome (3a): no bombardment, 41 sick landed, the weapons claim answered by a neutral signed report, no name released, talks possible. Illuminara's decisive contribution: she refuses to carry the words for Bram, asks what he heard rather than what he feared, goes to the ship to ask what it would never allow, and lets him choose the read-back himself.

This is a strong first draft whose moral and causal engine is exact speech rather than a speech about honesty. Bram refuses to counterfeit Quillan's answer, then uses read-back to discover Vey's actual constraint. Illuminara is decisive without taking over: she separates Bram's fear from what Vey actually said, asks the ship what it will never permit, and carries only Sefa's authorized terms. Quillan, Vey and Sefa retain real authority; the medical landing, neutral inspection and silent deadline deliver a meaningful positive result while dismissal, resentment, dissent and the distant blockade remain. Two load-bearing details need repair before the settlement is fully earned: the command's claim about a wanted man disappears after Vey names it, and the chronology does not yet show what verified event authorizes Vey to move six kilometres before Brightwater's signed report arrives.

AUTHOR_REVISION of S3 answering T02 P1 and P2 (both ACCEPTED). Preserved per the critic's protect list: the two-word refusal and three-word lie on the tide table, Illuminara asking what Vey said rather than what he feared, Bram's read-back distinguishing a yes from a reportable answer, Sefa's refusal of names, disclosure of the rifles, vote and sick-first, Quillan saying each term aloud, the quay observer, Brightwater's signed report, the six-kilometre partial withdrawal, the silent midnight, Bram's dismissal and Sefa asking for him by name. Speaking roles unchanged (Quillan, Bram, Vey, Illuminara, Sefa); Brightwater, Lask and the aide do not speak. Outcome (3a) unchanged and more complete: 41 sick landed, no bombardment, weapons claim answered by a neutral signed report, person claim answered by a sealed, privately asked question with a later hearing, no name released, talks possible; remaining costs: Bram dismissed from the delegation, Quillan resents the inspection, one voter on the ship stays angry, Vey's command may reject the process answer, the blockade remains at distance. R14 observation: the decisive turns are Sefa's 'a vote cannot give away a person' and the private self-answered question; Illuminara's capability is not used, her act is asking, carrying exactly and refusing to answer for anyone. Left for the critic: whether scene five is still too procedural now that it carries two claims plus a staged authority.

T03 visibly repairs both T02 priorities while preserving the draft's strongest living idea: exact language is not passivity but a way to discover what each person can honestly authorize. The person claim is now separated from the weapons claim; Sefa refuses to let a majority surrender a person; the ship authorizes only a private, neutral question with sealed self-answers; and Vey records that he holds no name. The cruiser movement is also tied to two observed triggers, logged discretion and a reversible condition before the full report. Bram, Sefa, Quillan and Vey all retain consequential authority, and Illuminara remains decisive through attention, exact carriage and refusal to speak for others. The story has reached a credible pre-final form. Two bounded proof details remain: state the evidentiary conclusion Vey can actually report without treating self-identification as proof, and make the concrete safety value of the six-kilometre partial withdrawal legible.

AUTHOR_FINAL of S3, answering T04 P1 and P2 (both ACCEPTED, no new plot, speaker or scene). Preserved per the critic's protect list: the two-word refusal and three-word lie on the tide table; Illuminara asking what Vey said rather than what he feared and refusing to compose Bram's question; Bram's read-back distinguishing a yes from a reportable answer; Sefa's refusal of names, disclosure of the rifles and 'a vote cannot give away a person'; Quillan saying each concession aloud; the paired movement triggers, the quay observer and the signed report; the silent midnight, Bram's dismissal and Sefa asking for him by name. Speaking roles unchanged: Quillan, Bram, Vey, Illuminara, Sefa. Outcome (3a): forty-one sick landed, rifles sealed by a neutral, no refugee name released, no bombardment, the weapons claim answered by a neutral signed report and the person claim kept at 'unproved' with a lawful hearing ahead, the harbour mouth open and warning time gained, talks possible. Remaining costs: Bram dismissed from the delegation, Quillan resents the inspection, one voter aboard stays angry, Vey's command may reject a process answer, the blockade remains at distance with the guns still in reach. R14 observation: the decisive turns are Sefa's refusal to let a majority give away a person, the private self-answered question, and Vey accepting a narrower, signable truth; Illuminara's capability is not used, her acts are asking, carrying exactly and refusing to answer for anyone.

T05 answers both bounded T04 priorities as visible source changes while preserving the story's exact-language core. P1: Vey explicitly refuses to call the sealed self-answers a finding, states that nobody has told him whether Lask is aboard, and narrows what he can sign to a verified neutral process, no ground for custody on the quay and an allegation that remains unproved rather than disproved. Bram reads that boundary back, and Brightwater's signed report repeats it without releasing a name or answer. P2: Quillan asks what six kilometres changes; Vey states that it opens the harbour mouth to pilot boats and ambulances, removes a gun laid directly on them and turns any renewed close approach into visible minutes rather than seconds, while admitting that the guns can still reach the quay. The final scene makes that benefit observable when a pilot boat exits before the cruiser has finished turning. At 3,394 recorded words the story remains within the normal range. R10 form passes: all six unnumbered scenes begin with an italic place/time line, and the body contains 77 properly separated bold-speaker dialogue blocks.

final_critic_line: By asking Bram to separate what was said from what he feared—and then refusing to put words in anyone's mouth—Illuminara helps a truthful refusal become medical access, a neutral process, an open harbour mouth and a silent midnight without surrendering a single refugee name.
